candidates.reason: vhost_get_vq_desc() (1992-2131), the primary host-side reader of guest-shared avail/desc memory. avail->idx fetched once via vhost_get_avail into local avail_idx and cached in vq->avail_idx with the wrap check '(u16)(vq->avail_idx - last_avail_idx) > vq->num' at 2015; ring_head fetched once into local at 2035-2036 and bounds-checked 'head >= vq->num' at 2046 before use as descriptor index; each descriptor is snapshotted with vhost_copy_from_user(vq, &desc, vq->desc + i, sizeof desc) at 2071-2072 and every subsequent desc.addr/desc.len/desc.next/desc.flags use (2078-2123) reads the LOCAL copy. translate_desc() consumes the local addr/len, not guest memory. No second dereference of guest memory after validation.

next_desc() reads desc->next via READ_ONCE at 1882 from the LOCAL snapshot struct copied by vhost_copy_from_user at 2071; the returned index is re-validated 'i >= vq->num' at 2060 before the next descriptor copy. Single fetch, validated local.

get_indirect() takes 'struct vring_desc *indirect' which points at the caller's local snapshot (passed &desc at 2081), reads indirect->len/indirect->addr from that local (1894, 1907), validates 'len % sizeof desc' at 1899 and count vs USHRT_MAX at 1923, and copies each indirect descriptor into a local via copy_from_iter_full at 1937; all inner desc.addr/desc.len/flags/next uses (1942-1978) are on the local copy. No guest re-dereference between check and use.

__vhost_add_used_n()/vhost_add_used_n() (2155-2230) only WRITE the guest-shared used ring via vhost_put_user/vhost_copy_to_user; the write index 'start = vq->last_used_idx & (vq->num - 1)' derives from kernel state, not from guest-shared memory, so there is no fetch-validate-refetch split.

vhost_enable_notify() (2320-2355), vhost_vq_avail_empty() (2302-2317) and vhost_notify() (2249-2269) each fetch avail->idx / avail->flags / used_event exactly once into a local (__virtio16 avail_idx / flags / event) via vhost_get_avail and use only that local for the boolean result or the cached vq->avail_idx heuristic; no validated value is refetched from the shared ring before use as a bound or pointer.

vhost_vq_init_access() fetches used->idx once with vhost_get_used at 1809 into local last_used_idx after access_ok at 1805, then stores it to vq->last_used_idx; the value is never re-read from guest memory for validation or use.

VHOST_SET_VRING_ADDR / VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM / VHOST_SET_VRING_BASE ioctl handlers (1380-1492) snapshot the request with copy_from_user into local 'a'/'s' and validate the LOCAL copy (alignment at 1458-1463, vq_access_ok at 1469-1475, num sanity at 1406); the stored vq->desc/avail/used pointers are then only re-validated via per-access __get_user fault handling plus per-iteration bounds checks in vhost_get_vq_desc, under vq->mutex which the TX workers also hold. No double fetch of a validated scalar.

__vringh_get_head() (32-70): avail->idx fetched once via the getu16 callback into local avail_idx; avail->ring[i] fetched once into local head; head is bounds-checked 'head >= vrh->vring.num' at 62-66 BEFORE being returned and used as the descriptor index. Single-fetch with validation on the fetched copy.

__vringh_iov() (254-399), used by both vringh_getdesc_user (copy_from_user via copydesc_user) and vringh_getdesc_kern (memcpy via copydesc_kern) against guest/shared rings: each descriptor is snapshotted into local 'struct vring_desc desc' at 290-293; every subsequent use of desc.flags/desc.addr/desc.len/desc.next (297-388) reads the LOCAL copy. Chained index is checked 'i >= desc_max' at 388-392 before the next copy at 293; indirect tables go through rcheck/range_check (303, 350) with truncation re-applied against the local desc.len at 368-373. No refetch of the shared ring between check and use.

Kern accessors getu16_kern (READ_ONCE(*p) at 824), copydesc_kern (memcpy snapshot at 836) and the user accessors getu16_user/get_user (555), copydesc_user/copy_from_user (566-570) each perform exactly one fetch into a local; there is no accessor that reads the same shared field twice or stores an unvalidated second read into kernel state. __vringh_complete (401-447) only writes the used ring using kernel-derived indices.

vop_virtio_add_device() initializes vrh with vringh_init_kern on a bidirectionally DMA-mapped ring (guest-writable), but all ring consumption goes through vringh_getdesc_kern/vringh_iov_pull_kern/vringh_iov_push_kern, which snapshot descriptors via copydesc_kern/memcpy into locals inside __vringh_iov; vop_vringh_copy operates on the local kiov, not on shared memory.

caif_virtio RX/TX uses vringh_getdesc_kern()/vringh_complete_kern()/vringh_iov_pull_kern(), i.e. the snapshotting vringh layer; no direct second dereference of the shared vring was found in cfv_rx/cfv_recv or the TX path (grep of vringh call sites at 257-346, 674-744).

limitations: drivers/vdpa does not exist in snapshots/s02, so the vdpa part of the branch could not be audited at all in this snapshot.

Per-driver consumers of the vhost iov arrays (drivers/vhost/net.c, scsi.c, vsock.c, test.c call sites of vhost_get_vq_desc at net.c:559/569/1014, scsi.c:453/834, test.c:56, vsock.c:119/370) were enumerated but only net.c was partially inspected; the iov entries they consume are built by translate_desc() from local descriptor copies clamped against umem nodes, so the invariant is expected to hold upstream of them.
Guest-side drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c and virt/kvm were only skimmed via grep for host-side vring readers; they implement the device side, which is out of this branch's trust direction.
Static source review only; no compilation or runtime race harness was run for s02.
